narrative:
The model estimated a 68.8% chance that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt, and because that risk was considered high, your law school application was denied.

The denial was driven primarily by your third-year class-rank decile, the strongest factor in the prediction. Your third-year decile was 1, far below the average of about 5.79 among accepted students, and this low standing pushed the prediction toward failure. Your LSAT score was the second most influential factor, and it helped you: at 41, it was above the accepted-student average of about 37.18, so it pushed toward passing. However, that positive signal was not enough to offset the academic-standing concerns. The third most important factor was your first-year class-rank decile; at 2, well below the accepted average of about 6, it also pushed toward failure. Together, the two low class-rank indicators outweighed your stronger LSAT.

To move forward, ask admissions for specific feedback, address any circumstances behind your low class ranks, and build a clear plan to strengthen your academic record before reapplying. You may also meet with an advisor to discuss whether retaking the LSAT or taking additional coursework would help demonstrate readiness, and consider programs where your overall profile is a better fit.
